title: Chicken Drumstick, Baked, Broiled, or Roasted, Skin Not Eaten

content.title: About
content.content: Skinless chicken drumsticks are the thigh meat of the bird, prepared by baking, broiling or roasting. Removing the skin reduces fat content while preserving a high amount of protein, B‑vitamins and minerals such as iron and zinc.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Drumsticks contain more iron than chicken breast because of the denser muscle fibers.
When cooked without skin, some fat renders out, which can make the meat drier; marinades or spices are often used to retain juiciness.
Chicken drumsticks are a staple in many cuisines, from American BBQ to Asian teriyaki dishes.
Thigh meat has a higher creatine content, supporting energy production in muscles.
Even without the skin, a well‑cooked drumstick can develop a pleasant crust when broiled.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: A 100 g serving provides about 22 g of complete protein, essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Without skin the total fat drops to 3–4 g per 100 g, making it suitable for lower‑fat diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Rich in niacin (B3) and vitamin B6, which support metabolism and nervous‑system function.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Provides iron, zinc and phosphorus, important for blood health, immunity and bone strength.

items.title: Creatine
items.content: Helps improve physical endurance and maintains cellular energy balance in muscles.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Raw chicken can harbor Salmonella or Campylobacter; cook to an internal temperature of 74 °C (165 °F) to ensure safety.

items.title: High sodium in marinades
items.content: Pre‑made marinades can be salty; monitor sodium intake if you have hypertension.

items.title: Dryness risk
items.content: Skinless drumsticks can become dry if overcooked; use a meat thermometer and avoid excessive cooking time.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Skinless drumsticks can be served as a main dish, sliced for salads, added to soups, or used in sandwiches. They pair well with herbs (rosemary, thyme), spices (paprika, garlic) and light sauces such as yogurt‑based dressings or lemon vinaigrette.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store raw meat in the refrigerator at + 1‑4 °C for up to 2 days. Cooked drumsticks keep in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 3 days or freeze for up to 3 months. Reheat cooked meat to an internal temperature of 74 °C before eating.
